title: Rent
tagline: No heat, no rent money. Dinner's on Angel.
about: In New York's East Village, a group of broke artist friends living in and around a freezing loft spend a year fighting their landlord, chasing their art and looking after each other.
cue: Serve the snacks when the power gets cut in Mark and Roger's loft on Christmas Eve.

    StartersAvenue B cart soft pretzels with mustardChewy, dark brown soft pretzels with coarse salt, served warm with yellow and wholegrain mustardHow to make it500g bread flour7g dried yeast1 tbsp sugar2 tsp salt30g butter, melted325ml warm water2 L water, for the bath80g bicarbonate of soda1 egg, beaten1 tbsp coarse sea salt4 tbsp yellow mustard4 tbsp wholegrain mustardMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, melted butter and warm water and knead until smooth.Cover and leave somewhere warm until doubled.Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the dough into 8, roll each into a long rope and twist into a pretzel.Boil the water for the bath with the bicarbonate of soda and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds, then lift onto lined trays.Brush with the egg, scatter with the coarse salt and bake until deep brown.Serve warm with the yellow and wholegrain mustard in bowls.Mark's film reel pinwheelsPuff pastry rolled with sun-dried tomato pesto, parmesan and cheddar, sliced and baked crispHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry, thawed3 tbsp sun-dried tomato pesto40g parmesan, grated80g cheddar, grated1 egg, beatenSpread the pastry sheets with the pesto and scatter over the parmesan and cheddar.Roll each sheet up tightly from the long side.Chill so the logs slice cleanly. Heat the oven to 200°C.Cut into 1.5cm rounds, lay flat on lined trays and brush with the egg.Bake until puffed and golden, then cool a few minutes.Seaweed salad with sesameOrdered by the dozen at the Life Café.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsChristmas Eve arroz con pollo for the loftGarlic and lime chicken thighs simmered in yellow sofrito rice with capsicum, green olives and peasHow to make it8 bone-in chicken thighs, skin on7 garlic cloves, 3 crushed for the rub, 4 for the sofrito1 tsp dried oregano1 tsp ground cumin2 limes, 1 juiced, 1 in wedges1 tsp salt1 brown onion, roughly chopped1 green capsicum, roughly chopped1 red capsicum, roughly chopped1 handful coriander2 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp tomato paste1 tsp sweet paprika1/2 tsp ground turmeric400g medium grain rice750ml chicken stock2 bay leaves1 cup frozen peas100g green olivesRub the chicken with the crushed garlic, oregano, cumin, lime juice and salt.Leave to marinate.Blitz the onion, both capsicums, the rest of the garlic and the coriander to a rough sofrito.Brown the chicken skin side down in the olive oil in a wide heavy pot, turning once, then lift out.Fry the sofrito in the fat until soft.Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, turmeric and rice.Pour in the stock, add the bay leaves, sit the chicken on top, cover and simmer gently.Scatter over the peas and olives, cover off the heat to finish, and serve with the lime wedges.Collins' Santa Fe green chilli pork stewCollins' big plan: leave the city and open a restaurant in Santa FeHow to make it1kg pork shoulder, diced4 long green chillies2 green capsicums1 onion, diced3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp ground cumin750ml chicken stock500g potatoes, diced8 flour tortillas1 lime1 bunch coriander2 tbsp olive oilChar the chillies and capsicums under the grill, then peel, seed and chop.Brown the pork in the oil in a heavy pot, add the onion, garlic and cumin and cook until soft.Add the chillies, capsicum and stock and simmer covered until the pork is tender.Add the potatoes and simmer until soft.Serve with warm tortillas, lime and coriander.SweetsAngel's Christmas temblequePuerto Rican coconut milk pudding, set cold until it wobbles and dusted with cinnamonHow to make it800ml coconut milk80g cornflour110g caster sugar1 pinch of salt1 cinnamon stick1 tsp vanilla extract1 tsp ground cinnamon1 tsp vegetable oil, for the mouldWhisk the cornflour into the coconut milk in a saucepan until smooth, then add the sugar, salt and cinnamon stick.Stir over medium heat until it boils and turns thick and glossy.Take off the heat, lift out the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla. Pour into a lightly oiled mould.Chill until set.Turn out onto a plate and dust with the ground cinnamon.DrinksCollins' hot toddy for a loft with no heatWhisky, honey and lemon with boiling water, steeped with cloves and cinnamon, in mugsHow to make it800ml water2 cinnamon sticks, broken in half8 whole cloves4 tbsp honey160ml whisky2 lemons, 1 juiced, 1 slicedSimmer the water with the cinnamon sticks and cloves.Put the honey and whisky into 4 heatproof mugs and squeeze in the lemon juice.Top with the hot spiced water and stir until the honey melts.Finish each mug with a lemon slice and a piece of the cinnamon stick.Pabst Blue Ribbon by the canLa Vie Boheme toast.
